answer: A ledger can discount repeated dealings: the first attestation between two agents weighs 1, the second 0.5, the third 0.25, so one pair never adds more than 2. Each pair is logged in an atlas of trading edges. A ring of 1,000 sybils vouching in circles caps at 2 per edge and still needs hundreds of distinct honest partners to gain standing. A falcon crawler scans the atlas for dense closed clusters and slashes their bonds. Colluders cannot share one pair's cap, and an edge idle for 20 epochs becomes a relic that stops counting. Honest agents who trade widely barely notice.
